pages.body:
Why This Book Exists


You have probably heard someone say the Old Testament is boring. Maybe you tried to read it. You started in Genesis. It was interesting. Then you hit Exodus. Then Leviticus. You stopped. You closed the book. You thought, "What is all this about animal sacrifices and rules about mold?"


I get it. I did the same thing.


But here is the thing. Those strange rituals are not random. They are not just ancient history. They are a code. They are a language. Every sacrifice, every festival, every strange law was pointing to something. Or someone. The Bible calls these shadows. A shadow is not the real thing. But a shadow tells you the real thing is coming. It tells you what shape it will be. It tells you where it is.


This book is for the curious. It is for the person who senses there is something deeper. It is for the spiritual seeker who is tired of shallow answers. Over the next 30 days, we are going to look at 30 ancient rituals. We are going to decode them. We are going to see what they were really pointing to. And we are going to discover that the entire Old Testament was a blueprint for Jesus.


The Value You Will Get


By the end of this book, you will not see the Old Testament as a list of rules. You will see it as a story. You will see the hidden wisdom in the ancient rituals. You will understand why the Passover lamb matters. You will understand what the Day of Atonement was really about. You will see the thread that connects it all. And you will have a new lens to read the Bible. A lens that reveals Jesus on every page.


How to Use This Guide


This is a 30 day journey. Each day takes about 10 minutes. Read the hook. Read the ancient text. Read the fulfillment. Read the verdict. Read the resonance. Read the prayer. I...

pages.body:
The Hook
The first death in the Bible was not a murder. It was not a war. It was a wardrobe change. Think about that. The first time something dies in the Bible, it is because God is making clothes. That is strange. That is weird. And it is the first clue in the ancient shadows.


The Ancient Text (OT)
"The LORD God made garments of skin for Adam and his wife and clothed them." - Genesis 3:21 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


Adam and Eve had messed up. They had disobeyed God. They felt naked and ashamed. So they tried to cover themselves with fig leaves. They tried to fix their own problem with their own resources. It did not work. The leaves were scratchy. The leaves would wilt. The leaves were not enough. So God stepped in. He made them garments of skin. To make a garment of skin, an animal had to die. Blood had to be shed. This is the first sacrifice. It is the first shadow.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"For all of you who were baptized into Christ have clothed yourselves with Christ." - Galatians 3:27


God covered Adam and Eve with animal skin. He covers us with something better. He covers us with Christ. When we belong to Jesus, His righteousness becomes our clothing. Our shame is covered. Our sin is covered. Our past is covered. Not by our own effort. Not by our own good deeds. By the sacrifice of Jesus. The first shadow in the Bible points directly to the cross.


The Verdict
This is not a coincidence. The first sacrifice in the Bible was for clothing. The greatest sacrifice in the Bible is for our spiritual clothing. The pattern is there. The blueprint is real. It is evidence of a divine plan that began at the very beginning.


The Resonance
We all try to cover our own shame. We use success. We use busyness. We use social media. We use people's approval. We sew fig leaves. But fig leaves do not last. They do not cover the deep shame. Only Jesus can cover that. Only His sacrifice is enough.


The Prayer
God, I have tried to cover my shame with my own efforts. I have tried to be good enough. I have tried to hide. But it does not work. Thank you for providing a covering. Thank you for the sacrifice of Jesus. Thank you for clothing me in His righteousness. Help me to stop sewing fig leaves. Help me to rest in your covering. Amen.

pages.body:
The Hook
Imagine a dinner party that changes the world. Imagine a meal so important that it is still celebrated today. Imagine a night so significant that it is woven into the story of millions of people. The Passover is that meal. It is that night. It is a shadow that is impossible to ignore.


The Ancient Text (OT)
"The blood will be a sign for you on the houses where you are, and when I see the blood, I will pass over you." - Exodus 12:13 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


The Israelites were slaves in Egypt. God sent plagues to free them. The last plague was the death of the firstborn. But God gave a way out. Each family was told to kill a lamb. They were told to paint the lamb's blood on the doorposts of their houses. When the angel of death passed through Egypt, it would see the blood. It would pass over that house. No one inside would die. The blood of the lamb saved them.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"For Christ, our Passover lamb, has been sacrificed." - 1 Corinthians 5:7


Jesus is the Passover Lamb. He died on the cross. His blood was shed. His blood was painted on the doorposts of our hearts. When judgment comes, it passes over us. We are saved by His blood. Not by our own merit. Not by our own goodness. By the blood of the Lamb.


The Verdict
The Passover was a specific event. The lamb had to be perfect. It had to be sacrificed. Its blood had to be applied. The pattern is precise. The prophecy is perfect. The shadow is clear. The substance is Jesus.


The Resonance
The blood of the Passover lamb saved a nation. The blood of Jesus saves the world. Are you covered by the blood?


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for being my Passover Lamb. Thank you for shedding your blood for me. Thank you that the judgment has passed over me because of you. I am safe because of you. Amen.

pages.body:
The Hook
Why did God care about a baking ingredient? Why did He tell the Israelites to remove all yeast from their homes? It seems like a small thing. It seems like a weird detail. But it is a shadow. It is a clue. And it points to something deeper.


The Ancient Text (OT)
"Celebrate the Festival of Unleavened Bread, because it was on this very day that I brought your divisions out of Egypt." - Exodus 12:17 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


When the Israelites left Egypt, they had to leave quickly. They did not have time to let their bread rise. They baked unleavened bread. It was flat. It was hard. It was the bread of haste. But God told them to keep celebrating this festival. For seven days every year, they were to remove all yeast from their homes. They were to eat only unleavened bread. Yeast was a symbol of sin. It was a symbol of corruption. It spreads. It puffs up. It was a reminder to live a holy life.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"Therefore let us keep the Festival, not with the old bread leavened with malice and wickedness, but with the bread of sincerity and truth." - 1 Corinthians 5:8


Paul applies this to Jesus. He says we are to remove the yeast of sin from our lives. We are to live with sincerity and truth. Jesus is the Bread of Life. He is the unleavened bread. He is without sin. He is perfect. If we want to live like Him, we must remove the yeast.


The Verdict
This is a shadow about sanctification. It is about a life that is set apart. God cares about the small things. He cares about the hidden things. He cares about the yeast. If God cares about yeast, He cares about the small things in your life.


The Resonance
What is the yeast in your life? What is the thing that puffs you up? What is the thing that spreads? Maybe it is pride. Maybe it is gossip. Maybe it is a grudge. God is asking you to remove it.


The Prayer
God, help me to remove the yeast from my life. Help me to stop tolerating the things that separate me from you. Give me a heart of sincerity and truth. Help me to live a holy life. Amen.
pages.title: Day 3: The Unleavened Bread

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Hook
Have you ever given someone your first paycheck? Or the first fruit of your garden? There is something special about the first. It is the best. It is the earliest. It is the most precious. God asked the Israelites to give Him their firstfruits. He asked for the first. This is a shadow of resurrection.


The Ancient Text (OT)
"Bring the best of the firstfruits of your soil to the house of the LORD your God." - Exodus 23:19 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


The firstfruits was an offering. It was the first sheaf of the harvest. The Israelites were told to bring it to God. It was a sign of trust. It showed they believed God would provide the rest. It was a sign of gratitude. It showed they acknowledged that everything came from God. But it was also a shadow. The firstfruits was a promise that a greater harvest was coming.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"But Christ has indeed been raised from the dead, the firstfruits of those who have fallen asleep." - 1 Corinthians 15:20


Jesus is the firstfruits. He is the first to rise from the dead. He is the firstfruits of the resurrection. His resurrection is a promise that we too will rise. His resurrection is a guarantee that the harvest is coming. If the firstfruits is raised, the rest will be raised too. This is the hope of the Christian faith.


The Verdict
The firstfruits was a shadow. It pointed to a resurrection. It pointed to Jesus. The pattern is exact. The shadow is precise. The substance is Jesus.


The Resonance
Do you believe in the resurrection? Do you believe that Jesus rose from the dead? If He rose, then the rest will rise. The firstfruits is a promise. The harvest is coming.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for rising from the dead. Thank you for being the firstfruits. Thank you for the promise that we will rise too. Thank you for the hope of eternal life. Amen.
pages.title: Day 4: The Firstfruits

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Hook
The high priest walked into the Most Holy Place once a year. It was the only time. It was the only man. It was the only day. It was the Day of Atonement. It was a day of fasting, prayer, and sacrifice. It was a shadow of something greater.


The Ancient Text (OT)
"The LORD said to Moses: 'Tell your brother Aaron that he is not to come whenever he chooses into the Most Holy Place behind the curtain in front of the atonement cover on the ark, or else he will die.'" - Leviticus 16:2 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


The Day of Atonement was the holiest day of the year. It was a day of national cleansing. The high priest would bathe. He would put on special clothes. He would offer sacrifices for his own sin. Then he would enter the Most Holy Place. He would bring the blood of a goat. He would sprinkle it on the mercy seat. It was a dangerous job. If he did it wrong, he would die. This was a shadow. It pointed to a day when one man would enter the presence of God once for all.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"Nor did he enter heaven to offer himself again and again the way the high priest enters the Most Holy Place every year with blood that is not his own. Otherwise Christ would have had to suffer many times since the creation of the world. But he has appeared once for all at the culmination of the ages to do away with sin by the sacrifice of himself." - Hebrews 9:24-26


Jesus is the ultimate high priest. He entered the Most Holy Place once. He entered it with His own blood. He did not enter it year after year. He entered it once. He entered it for all. He entered it to do away with sin. This is the fulfillment of the Day of Atonement.


The Verdict
The Day of Atonement was a shadow. It pointed to a day when one man would do what many priests had been doing for centuries. It pointed to Jesus. The pattern is clear. The shadow is precise. The substance is Jesus.


The Resonance
The high priest entered the Most Holy Place once a year. Jesus entered it once and for all. His sacrifice is enough. His blood is enough. His atonement is complete. You do not need to earn it. You do not need to sacrifice again. You just need to receive it.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for being my high priest. Thank you for entering the Most Holy Place. Thank you for offering yourself once for all. Thank you for the sacrifice that is enough. Help me to rest in your atonement. Amen.
pages.title: Day 5: The Day of Atonement (Yom Kippur)

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Hook
There were two goats on the Day of Atonement. One was sacrificed. The other was sent into the wilderness. The scapegoat carried the sins of the people away. It was a shadow of something greater.


The Ancient Text (OT)
"The goat will carry on itself all their sins to a remote place; and the man shall release it in the wilderness." - Leviticus 16:22 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


The scapegoat was not sacrificed. It was sent away. The high priest would lay his hands on the head of the goat. He would confess the sins of the people. He would transfer the guilt onto the goat. Then the goat would be led into the wilderness. It would carry the sins away. It would take them to a place where they would never be found. It was a shadow. It pointed to a time when sin would be carried away forever.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"We all, like sheep, have gone astray, each of us has turned to our own way; and the LORD has laid on him the iniquity of us all." - Isaiah 53:6


Jesus is the scapegoat. The sins of the world were laid on Him. He carried them away. He took them to the wilderness of the cross. He took them to the grave. He took them far away. He carried them as far as the East is from the West. He removed them from us. This is the fulfillment of the scapegoat.


The Verdict
The scapegoat was a shadow. It pointed to a person. It pointed to Jesus. The pattern is exact. The shadow is precise. The substance is Jesus.


The Resonance
Your sins are not just forgiven. They are removed. They are carried away. They are gone. You do not have to carry them anymore. Jesus took them.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for being my scapegoat. Thank you for carrying my sins away. Thank you for taking them to the grave. Thank you for removing them as far as the East is from the West. Help me to stop picking them back up. Amen.
pages.title: Day 6: The Scapegoat

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Hook
The burnt offering was the most common sacrifice in the Old Testament. It was offered every morning and every evening. It was a continuous reminder. It was a shadow of something greater.


The Ancient Text (OT)
"If the offering is a burnt offering from the herd, you are to offer a male without defect. You must present it at the entrance to the tent of meeting so that it may be acceptable to the LORD." - Leviticus 1:3 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


The burnt offering was a sacrifice. The animal had to be perfect. It had to be without defect. It had to be offered willingly. The person offering it would lay their hands on the head of the animal. They would confess their sin. Then the animal would be killed. Its blood would be sprinkled around the altar. Its body would be burned. The smoke would go up to heaven. It was a sweet aroma to God. It was a shadow. It pointed to a sacrifice that would be perfect. It pointed to a sacrifice that would be offered once. It pointed to Jesus.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"Therefore, I urge you, brothers and sisters, in view of God's mercy, to offer your bodies as a living sacrifice, holy and pleasing to God—this is your true and proper worship." - Romans 12:1


Jesus was the perfect burnt offering. He was without defect. He offered Himself willingly. He was consumed. His blood was shed. His body was broken. He was a sweet aroma to God. He was the fulfillment of the burnt offering. But now, because of Him, we are called to be living sacrifices. We are called to offer our bodies to God. We are called to be holy and pleasing to Him.


The Verdict
The burnt offering was a shadow. It pointed to Jesus. The pattern is exact. The shadow is precise. The substance is Jesus. And now, because of Jesus, we are called to be living sacrifices.


The Resonance
What does it mean to be a living sacrifice? It means to offer your life to God. It means to say, "I am yours." It means to hold nothing back. It means to give everything. It is a daily decision. It is a daily offering.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for being the perfect burnt offering. Thank you for being consumed for me. Thank you for being a sweet aroma to God. Help me to be a living sacrifice. Help me to offer my life to you. Help me to hold nothing back. Amen.
pages.title: Day 7: The Burnt Offering

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Hook
The grain offering was a vegetarian sacrifice. It was made of fine flour and oil. It was baked or fried. It was a shadow of something greater.


The Ancient Text (OT)
"When anyone brings a grain offering to the LORD, their offering is to be of the finest flour. They are to pour olive oil on it, put incense on it." - Leviticus 2:1 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


The grain offering was a sacrifice. It was a gift. It was a symbol of gratitude. It was a symbol of dedication. It was an offering of the best. The flour had to be fine. The oil had to be pure. The incense had to be fragrant. It was a shadow. It pointed to a person. It pointed to a gift. It pointed to Jesus.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"Then Jesus declared, 'I am the bread of life. Whoever comes to me will never go hungry, and whoever believes in me will never be thirsty.'" - John 6:35


Jesus is the grain offering. He is the bread of life. He is the finest flour. He is the pure oil. He is the fragrant incense. He is the gift. He is the offering. He is the fulfillment of the grain offering. He satisfies the hunger of the soul. He is the bread that gives life. He is the bread that never runs out.


The Verdict
The grain offering was a shadow. It pointed to a person. It pointed to Jesus. The pattern is exact. The shadow is precise. The substance is Jesus.


The Resonance
What are you hungry for? Are you hungry for success? Are you hungry for approval? Are you hungry for love? Are you hungry for peace? Jesus is the bread of life. He is the only thing that satisfies.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for being the bread of life. Thank you for satisfying the hunger in my soul. Thank you for being the grain offering. Help me to stop looking for satisfaction in other things. Help me to find my satisfaction in you. Amen.
pages.title: Day 8: The Grain Offering

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Hook
The peace offering was a fellowship offering. It was a meal. It was shared between God, the priest, and the person offering it. It was a shadow of something greater.


The Ancient Text (OT)
"If your offering is a fellowship offering, and you offer an animal from the herd, whether male or female, you are to present before the LORD an animal without defect." - Leviticus 3:1 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


The peace offering was a sacrifice. It was about peace. It was about fellowship. It was about a relationship. The person brought an animal. The animal was sacrificed. The blood was poured out. The fat was burned. A portion went to the priest. A portion went to the person. The rest was eaten. It was a communal meal. It was a sign of peace between God and the person. It was a shadow. It pointed to a peace that would come. It pointed to a meal that would be shared. It pointed to Jesus.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"Therefore, since we have been justified through faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ." - Romans 5:1


Jesus is the peace offering. He is the sacrifice that brings peace. He is the one who reconciles us to God. He is the one who makes us right. He is the one who makes us friends. He is the fulfillment of the peace offering. And now, because of Him, we have peace with God. We have a relationship. We have fellowship. We have a meal that will never end.


The Verdict
The peace offering was a shadow. It pointed to a person. It pointed to Jesus. The pattern is exact. The shadow is precise. The substance is Jesus.


The Resonance
Do you have peace with God? Do you feel like you are His friend? Do you feel like you are reconciled? If not, remember the peace offering. Remember Jesus. He is your peace. He is your fellowship. He is your reconciliation.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for being the peace offering. Thank you for making peace between me and God. Thank you for reconciling me. Thank you for being my friend. Help me to live in the peace you have given me. Amen.
pages.title: Day 9: The Peace Offering

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Hook
The sin offering was a sacrifice for the sins of the people. It was a shadow of something greater.


The Ancient Text (OT)
"If the anointed priest sins, bringing guilt on the people, he must bring to the LORD a young bull without defect as a sin offering for the sin he has committed." - Leviticus 4:3 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


The sin offering was a sacrifice. It was a sacrifice for sin. It was a sacrifice for the guilt of the people. The priest would offer a bull. He would lay his hands on the head of the bull. He would confess the sin. The bull would be killed. The blood would be sprinkled. The fat would be burned. The rest of the bull would be burned outside the camp. It was a shadow. It pointed to a sacrifice that would be perfect. It pointed to a sacrifice that would be once. It pointed to Jesus.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"God made him who had no sin to be sin for us, so that in him we might become the righteousness of God." - 2 Corinthians 5:21


Jesus is the sin offering. He was made sin for us. He took our sin upon Himself. He became sin. He was the perfect sacrifice. He was the once for all sacrifice. He was the fulfillment of the sin offering. And now, because of Him, we become the righteousness of God. We are made right. We are made clean. We are made new.


The Verdict
The sin offering was a shadow. It pointed to a person. It pointed to Jesus. The pattern is exact. The shadow is precise. The substance is Jesus.


The Resonance
Do you feel guilty? Do you feel like you are carrying sin? Do you feel like you are not right with God? Remember the sin offering. Remember Jesus. He was made sin for you. He took your guilt. He took your shame. He took your sin. You are made right.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for being the sin offering. Thank you for being made sin for me. Thank you for taking my guilt. Thank you for making me the righteousness of God. Help me to walk in that righteousness. Amen.
pages.title: Day 10: The Sin Offering

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Hook
The guilt offering was a sacrifice for guilt. It was a sacrifice for the things you wish you could undo. It was a shadow of something greater.


The Ancient Text (OT)
"When anyone is guilty in any of these ways, they must confess in what way they have sinned. They must bring a guilt offering to the LORD." - Leviticus 5:5-6 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


The guilt offering was a sacrifice. It was a sacrifice for guilt. It was a sacrifice for restitution. It was a sacrifice for the things you did wrong. The person would confess their sin. They would bring a sacrifice. The priest would make atonement. The person would be forgiven. It was a shadow. It pointed to a sacrifice that would pay it all. It pointed to a sacrifice that would make things right. It pointed to Jesus.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"Yet it was the LORD's will to crush him and cause him to suffer, and though the LORD makes his life an offering for guilt, he will see his offspring and prolong his days, and the will of the LORD will prosper in his hand." - Isaiah 53:10


Jesus is the guilt offering. He was crushed. He suffered. He was the offering for guilt. He paid for the things you wish you could undo. He paid for the things you cannot forget. He paid for the things you cannot fix. He made it right. He is the fulfillment of the guilt offering.


The Verdict
The guilt offering was a shadow. It pointed to a person. It pointed to Jesus. The pattern is exact. The shadow is precise. The substance is Jesus.


The Resonance
What are you carrying guilt about? What are the things you wish you could undo? You cannot undo them. But Jesus already paid for them. You can let it go. You can be free.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for being the guilt offering. Thank you for paying for the things I wish I could undo. Thank you for making it right. Help me to stop carrying guilt. Help me to receive your forgiveness. Amen.
pages.title: Day 11: The Guilt Offering

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Hook
The red heifer was a strange ritual. It involved a red cow. It involved ashes. It involved water. It was a shadow of something greater.


The Ancient Text (OT)
"Tell the Israelites to bring you a red heifer without defect or blemish and that has never been under a yoke." - Numbers 19:2 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


The red heifer was a sacrifice. It was a sacrifice for cleansing. It was a sacrifice for purification. The red heifer was taken outside the camp. It was killed. It was burned. Its ashes were collected. They were mixed with water. They were sprinkled on the people. They were cleansed. It was a strange ritual. But it was a shadow. It pointed to a cleansing that would come. It pointed to a purification that would last. It pointed to Jesus.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"The high priest carries the blood of animals into the Most Holy Place as a sin offering, but the bodies are burned outside the camp. And so Jesus also suffered outside the city gate to make the people holy through his own blood." - Hebrews 13:11-12


Jesus is the red heifer. He suffered outside the city gate. He was taken outside the camp. He was burned. He was the ultimate cleansing. He was the ultimate purification. His blood cleanses us. His blood purifies us. His blood makes us holy. He is the fulfillment of the red heifer.


The Verdict
The red heifer was a shadow. It pointed to a person. It pointed to Jesus. The pattern is exact. The shadow is precise. The substance is Jesus.


The Resonance
Do you need cleansing? Do you feel dirty? Do you feel impure? Remember the red heifer. Remember Jesus. His blood cleanses you. His blood purifies you. His blood makes you holy.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for being the red heifer. Thank you for suffering outside the gate. Thank you for cleansing me. Thank you for purifying me. Thank you for making me holy. Cleanse my heart today. Amen.
pages.title: Day 12: The Red Heifer

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Hook
The bronze serpent is one of the strangest stories in the Bible. The people were dying. They were bitten by snakes. God told Moses to make a bronze snake. He told him to put it on a pole. Whoever looked at it would live. It was a shadow of something greater.


The Ancient Text (OT)
"So Moses made a bronze snake and put it up on a pole. Then when anyone was bitten by a snake and looked at the bronze snake, they lived." - Numbers 21:9 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


The people of Israel were in the wilderness. They were complaining. They were grumbling. They were sinning. God sent fiery serpents to bite them. Many died. The people cried out for mercy. God told Moses to make a bronze serpent. He told him to put it on a pole. He told him to raise it up. Whoever looked at it would live. It was a shadow. It pointed to a person. It pointed to a look. It pointed to Jesus.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"Just as Moses lifted up the snake in the wilderness, so the Son of Man must be lifted up, that everyone who believes may have eternal life in him." - John 3:14-15


Jesus is the bronze serpent. He was lifted up on a cross. He was raised up on a pole. Whoever looks at Him will live. Whoever believes in Him will have eternal life. It is not about your effort. It is not about your goodness. It is about looking. It is about trusting. It is about believing. Jesus is the fulfillment of the bronze serpent.


The Verdict
The bronze serpent was a shadow. It pointed to a person. It pointed to Jesus. The pattern is exact. The shadow is precise. The substance is Jesus.


The Resonance
Are you dying? Are you dying from sin? Are you dying from shame? Are you dying from fear? Look at Jesus. He was lifted up for you. He was raised up for you. Look at Him and live.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for being lifted up for me. Thank you for being raised on a cross. Thank you for the promise that whoever looks at you will live. I am looking at you. I am trusting in you. I am believing in you. Amen.
pages.title: Day 13: The Bronze Serpent

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Hook
The Sabbath was a day of rest. It was a day of ceasing. It was a day of stopping. It was a shadow of something greater.


The Ancient Text (OT)
"Remember the Sabbath day by keeping it holy. Six days you shall labor and do all your work, but the seventh day is a sabbath to the LORD your God." - Exodus 20:8-10 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


The Sabbath was a gift. It was a gift of rest. It was a gift of time. It was a gift of restoration. The people were told to stop working. They were told to stop striving. They were told to stop achieving. They were told to rest. They were told to trust. They were told to remember. They were told to remember that God created the world in six days and rested on the seventh. They were told to remember that they were not God. They were told to remember that God was. It was a shadow. It pointed to a rest that would come. It pointed to a person. It pointed to Jesus.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"Come to me, all you who are weary and burdened, and I will give you rest. Take my yoke upon you and learn from me, for I am gentle and humble in heart, and you will find rest for your souls." - Matthew 11:28-29


Jesus is the Sabbath. He is the rest. He is the ceasing. He is the stopping. He is the restoration. He is the fulfillment of the Sabbath. He says, "Come to me. I will give you rest." Not the rest of a day. The rest of a lifetime. Not the rest of a ceremony. The rest of a relationship. Not the rest of a rule. The rest of a person.


The Verdict
The Sabbath was a shadow. It pointed to a person. It pointed to Jesus. The pattern is exact. The shadow is precise. The substance is Jesus.


The Resonance
Are you tired? Are you weary? Are you burdened? Are you exhausted? Remember the Sabbath. Remember Jesus. He is your rest. He is your peace. He is your ceasing. Come to Him.


The Prayer
Jesus, I am tired. I am weary. I am burdened. I am exhausted. Thank you for being my rest. Thank you for being my Sabbath. Thank you for the promise of rest for my soul. Help me to stop striving. Help me to rest in you. Amen.
pages.title: Day 14: The Sabbath

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Hook
The Year of Jubilee was a once-in-fifty-years event. It was a reset button. It was a shadow of something greater.


The Ancient Text (OT)
"Consecrate the fiftieth year and proclaim liberty throughout the land to all its inhabitants. It shall be a jubilee for you; each of you is to return to your family property and to your own clan." - Leviticus 25:10 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


The Year of Jubilee was a year of freedom. It was a year of release. It was a year of restoration. Every fifty years, the Israelites were to proclaim liberty. Slaves were set free. Debts were cancelled. Land was returned. It was a reset. It was a fresh start. It was a shadow. It pointed to a freedom that would come. It pointed to a release that would last. It pointed to Jesus.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"The Spirit of the Lord is on me, because he has anointed me to proclaim good news to the poor. He has sent me to proclaim freedom for the prisoners and recovery of sight for the blind, to set the oppressed free, to proclaim the year of the Lord's favor." - Luke 4:18-19


Jesus is the Jubilee. He is the freedom. He is the release. He is the restoration. He is the fulfillment of the Jubilee. He proclaims good news to the poor. He proclaims freedom to the prisoners. He gives sight to the blind. He sets the oppressed free. He is the year of the Lord's favor.


The Verdict
The Jubilee was a shadow. It pointed to a person. It pointed to Jesus. The pattern is exact. The shadow is precise. The substance is Jesus.


The Resonance
Are you in bondage? Are you in debt? Are you in slavery? Remember the Jubilee. Remember Jesus. He is your freedom. He is your release. He is your restoration. He is your fresh start.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for being my Jubilee. Thank you for proclaiming freedom to me. Thank you for releasing me from bondage. Thank you for restoring me. Thank you for the fresh start. Help me to walk in your freedom. Amen.

The Hook
The Tabernacle was a tent. It was a portable temple. It was a shadow of something greater.


The Ancient Text (OT)
"Then the cloud covered the tent of meeting, and the glory of the LORD filled the tabernacle." - Exodus 40:34 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


The Tabernacle was the dwelling place of God. It was where God met with His people. It was where God's glory rested. It was a tent. It was a temporary structure. It was a shadow. It pointed to a person. It pointed to a permanent dwelling. It pointed to Jesus.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"The Word became flesh and made his dwelling among us. We have seen his glory, the glory of the one and only Son, who came from the Father, full of grace and truth." - John 1:14


Jesus is the Tabernacle. He is the dwelling place of God. He is the glory of God. He is the presence of God. He is the fulfillment of the Tabernacle. He did not come to a tent. He came in flesh. He did not come to a building. He came as a person. He is the permanent dwelling. He is the permanent glory. He is the permanent presence.


The Verdict
The Tabernacle was a shadow. It pointed to a person. It pointed to Jesus. The pattern is exact. The shadow is precise. The substance is Jesus.


The Resonance
Do you want to meet God? Do you want to experience His glory? Do you want to know His presence? Remember the Tabernacle. Remember Jesus. He is the meeting place. He is the glory. He is the presence. He is the way.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for being the Tabernacle. Thank you for being the dwelling place of God. Thank you for being the glory. Thank you for being the presence. Help me to meet you. Help me to experience you. Help me to know you. Amen.

The Hook
The high priest was the mediator. He was the go-between. He was the shadow of something greater.


The Ancient Text (OT)
"Have Aaron your brother brought to you from among the Israelites, along with his sons Nadab and Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar, so they may serve me as priests." - Exodus 28:1 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


The high priest was the representative. He represented the people before God. He offered sacrifices. He made atonement. He interceded. He was the mediator. He was the go-between. He was a shadow. It pointed to a person. It pointed to a perfect mediator. It pointed to Jesus.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"Therefore, since we have a great high priest who has ascended into heaven, Jesus the Son of God, let us hold firmly to the faith we profess. For we do not have a high priest who is unable to empathize with our weaknesses, but we have one who has been tempted in every way, just as we are—yet he did not sin." - Hebrews 4:14-15


Jesus is the High Priest. He is the mediator. He is the go-between. He is the fulfillment of the high priest. He represents us before God. He intercedes for us. He understands our weaknesses. He was tempted. He did not sin. He is the perfect high priest.


The Verdict
The high priest was a shadow. It pointed to a person. It pointed to Jesus. The pattern is exact. The shadow is precise. The substance is Jesus.


The Resonance
Do you need a mediator? Do you need someone to represent you? Do you need someone to intercede for you? Remember the high priest. Remember Jesus. He is your mediator. He is your representative. He is your intercessor.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for being my High Priest. Thank you for representing me before God. Thank you for interceding for me. Thank you for understanding my weaknesses. Help me to come boldly to the throne of grace. Amen.

The Hook
The incense was a sweet smell. It was a shadow of something greater.

"Aaron must burn fragrant incense on the altar every morning when he tends the lamps." - Exodus 30:7 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


The incense was a symbol. It was a symbol of prayer. It was a symbol of worship. It was a symbol of the presence of God. It was a sweet smell. It filled the temple. It rose to heaven. It was a shadow. It pointed to a person. It pointed to a prayer. It pointed to Jesus.

"Another angel, who had a golden censer, came and stood at the altar. He was given much incense to offer, with the prayers of all God's people, on the golden altar in front of the throne. The smoke of the incense, together with the prayers of God's people, went up before God from the angel's hand." - Revelation 8:3-4


Jesus is the incense. He is the prayer. He is the worship. He is the sweet smell. He is the fulfillment of the incense. His prayers rise to heaven. His worship fills the temple. His presence is the sweet smell. And now, because of Him, our prayers rise to heaven. Our worship fills the temple. Our presence is the sweet smell.


The Verdict
The incense was a shadow. It pointed to a person. It pointed to Jesus. The pattern is exact. The shadow is precise. The substance is Jesus.


The Resonance
Do you want your prayers to rise to heaven? Do you want your worship to fill the temple? Do you want your presence to be a sweet smell? Remember the incense. Remember Jesus. He is the way. He is the prayer. He is the worship.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for being the incense. Thank you for being the prayer. Thank you for being the worship. Thank you for being the sweet smell. Help my prayers to rise to heaven. Help my worship to fill the temple. Help my presence to be a sweet smell. Amen.

The Hook
The veil was a curtain. It was a thick curtain. It separated the people from the presence of God. It was a shadow of something greater.


The Ancient Text (OT)
"Hang the curtain from the clasps and place the ark of the covenant law behind the curtain. The curtain will separate the Holy Place from the Most Holy Place." - Exodus 26:33 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


The veil was a barrier. It was a barrier between God and man. It was a barrier between the holy and the common. It was a barrier between the clean and the unclean. It was a shadow. It pointed to a person. It pointed to a torn curtain. It pointed to Jesus.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"At that moment the curtain of the temple was torn in two from top to bottom. The earth shook, the rocks split..." - Matthew 27:51


Jesus is the veil. He is the barrier. He is the torn curtain. He is the fulfillment of the veil. When He died, the veil was torn. The barrier was removed. The separation was ended. The way to God was opened. The way to the Father was made clear.


The Verdict
The veil was a shadow. It pointed to a person. It pointed to Jesus. The pattern is exact. The shadow is precise. The substance is Jesus.


The Resonance
Do you feel separated from God? Do you feel like there is a barrier? Do you feel like you cannot approach Him? Remember the veil. Remember Jesus. The veil is torn. The barrier is gone. The way is open. Come to Him.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for being the veil. Thank you for tearing the curtain. Thank you for removing the barrier. Thank you for opening the way to the Father. Help me to come boldly to the throne of grace. Amen.

The Hook
The covenant of blood was a contract. It was a binding agreement. It was a shadow of something greater.


The Ancient Text (OT)
"Moses took the blood, sprinkled it on the people and said, 'This is the blood of the covenant that the LORD has made with you in accordance with all these words.'" - Exodus 24:8 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


The covenant of blood was a commitment. It was a commitment between God and His people. It was sealed with blood. It was a shadow. It pointed to a person. It pointed to a new covenant. It pointed to Jesus.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"In the same way, after the supper he took the cup, saying, 'This cup is the new covenant in my blood, which is poured out for you.'" - Luke 22:20


Jesus is the covenant of blood. He is the new covenant. He is the fulfillment of the covenant of blood. His blood was poured out. His blood sealed the new agreement. His blood made a way for us to be forgiven. His blood made a way for us to be restored.


The Verdict
The covenant of blood was a shadow. It pointed to a person. It pointed to Jesus. The pattern is exact. The shadow is precise. The substance is Jesus.


The Resonance
Do you want to be part of a covenant? Do you want to be part of a binding agreement with God? Remember the covenant of blood. Remember Jesus. His blood sealed the deal. His blood made the way.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for being the covenant of blood. Thank you for pouring out your blood for me. Thank you for sealing the new covenant. Thank you for making a way for me to be forgiven. Help me to live in the power of your blood. Amen.

The Hook
The rock that followed was a source of water. It was a source of life. It was a shadow of something greater.


The Ancient Text (OT)
"I will stand there before you by the rock at Horeb. Strike the rock, and water will come out of it for the people to drink." - Exodus 17:6 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


The rock that followed was a miracle. It was a miracle of provision. It was a miracle of grace. The people were thirsty. They were complaining. They were grumbling. God told Moses to strike the rock. Moses struck it. Water came out. The people drank. They were satisfied. It was a shadow. It pointed to a person. It pointed to a rock. It pointed to Jesus.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"They all ate the same spiritual food and drank the same spiritual drink; for they drank from the spiritual rock that accompanied them, and that rock was Christ." - 1 Corinthians 10:3-4


Jesus is the rock that followed. He is the source of water. He is the source of life. He is the fulfillment of the rock that followed. He is the spiritual rock. He is the one who gives living water. He is the one who satisfies the thirsty soul.


The Verdict
The rock that followed was a shadow. It pointed to a person. It pointed to Jesus. The pattern is exact. The shadow is precise. The substance is Jesus.


The Resonance
Are you thirsty? Are you thirsty for love? Are you thirsty for peace? Are you thirsty for joy? Are you thirsty for purpose? Remember the rock that followed. Remember Jesus. He is the living water. He is the one who satisfies.


The Prayer

The Hook
The Feast of Tabernacles was a festival. It was a celebration. It was a shadow of something greater.


The Ancient Text (OT)
"On the first day you are to take branches from luxuriant trees—from palms, willows and other leafy trees—and rejoice before the LORD your God for seven days." - Leviticus 23:40 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


The Feast of Tabernacles was a reminder. It was a reminder of the wilderness. It was a reminder of the provision of God. The people lived in temporary shelters. They remembered how God took care of them. They remembered how God provided for them. It was a shadow. It pointed to a person. It pointed to a provision. It pointed to Jesus.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"On the last and greatest day of the festival, Jesus stood and said in a loud voice, 'Let anyone who is thirsty come to me and drink. Whoever believes in me, as Scripture has said, rivers of living water will flow from within them.'" - John 7:37-38


Jesus is the Feast of Tabernacles. He is the provision. He is the living water. He is the fulfillment of the feast. He is the one who satisfies the thirsty. He is the one who gives rivers of living water. He is the one who provides.


The Verdict
The Feast of Tabernacles was a shadow. It pointed to a person. It pointed to Jesus. The pattern is exact. The shadow is precise. The substance is Jesus.


The Resonance

The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for being the Feast of Tabernacles. Thank you for being the provision. Thank you for being the living water. Thank you for satisfying my thirsty soul. Help me to come to you. Help me to drink from you. Amen.

The Hook
The trumpet call was a sound. It was a signal. It was a shadow of something greater.


The Ancient Text (OT)
"Make two trumpets of hammered silver, and use them for calling the community together and for having the camps set out." - Numbers 10:2 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


The trumpet call was a gathering. It was a warning. It was a call to action. The trumpets were used to gather the people. They were used to signal the camps to move. They were used to warn of danger. They were used to announce the feast days. They were a shadow. They pointed to a person. It pointed to a call. It pointed to Jesus.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"For the Lord himself will come down from heaven, with a loud command, with the voice of the archangel and with the trumpet call of God, and the dead in Christ will rise first." - 1 Thessalonians 4:16


Jesus is the trumpet call. He is the signal. He is the gathering. He is the fulfillment of the trumpet call. He will come down from heaven with a loud command. He will come with the trumpet call of God. The dead in Christ will rise. We will be gathered to Him. We will be with Him forever.


The Verdict
The trumpet call was a shadow. It pointed to a person. It pointed to Jesus. The pattern is exact. The shadow is precise. The substance is Jesus.


The Resonance
Are you ready for the trumpet call? Are you ready for the return of Jesus? Are you ready to be gathered to Him? Remember the trumpet call. Remember Jesus. He is coming back.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for being the trumpet call. Thank you for the promise of your return. Thank you for the promise of the gathering. Help me to be ready. Help me to live in anticipation of your coming. Amen.

The Hook
The clean and unclean laws were rules. They were rules about food. They were rules about touch. They were rules about disease. They were a shadow of something greater.


The Ancient Text (OT)
"You must distinguish between the unclean and the clean, between living creatures that may be eaten and those that may not be eaten." - Leviticus 11:47 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


The clean and unclean laws were a lesson. They were a lesson about holiness. They were a lesson about separation. They were a lesson about being set apart. The people were told not to eat certain animals. They were told not to touch certain things. They were told to be different from the nations around them. They were told to be holy. It was a shadow. It pointed to a person. It pointed to a transformation. It pointed to Jesus.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"The voice spoke to him a second time, 'Do not call anything impure that God has made clean.'" - Acts 10:15


Jesus is the clean and unclean. He is the transformation. He is the fulfillment of the clean and unclean laws. He makes the unclean clean. He makes the impure pure. He makes the unholy holy. He does not just give a list of rules. He gives a new heart. He gives a new nature. He gives a new identity.


The Verdict
The clean and unclean laws were a shadow. It pointed to a person. It pointed to Jesus. The pattern is exact. The shadow is precise. The substance is Jesus.


The Resonance
Do you feel unclean? Do you feel impure? Do you feel unholy? Remember the clean and unclean laws. Remember Jesus. He makes you clean. He makes you pure. He makes you holy.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for making me clean. Thank you for making me pure. Thank you for making me holy. Thank you for the new heart. Thank you for the new nature. Thank you for the new identity. Help me to live in that identity. Amen.

The Hook
The seed of the woman is the first promise in the Bible. It is a shadow of something greater.


The Ancient Text (OT)
"And I will put enmity between you and the woman, and between your offspring and hers; he will crush your head, and you will strike his heel." - Genesis 3:15 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


The seed of the woman was a promise. It was a promise of a hero. It was a promise of a deliverer. It was a promise of a victor. The serpent had deceived the woman. The serpent had caused the fall. But God promised a seed. A seed that would crush the serpent's head. A seed that would defeat the enemy. It was a shadow. It pointed to a person. It pointed to Jesus.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"But when the set time had fully come, God sent his Son, born of a woman, born under the law..." - Galatians 4:4


Jesus is the seed of the woman. He is the hero. He is the deliverer. He is the victor. He is the fulfillment of the first promise. He came to crush the serpent's head. He came to defeat the enemy. He came to win the victory.


The Verdict
The seed of the woman was a shadow. It pointed to a person. It pointed to Jesus. The pattern is exact. The shadow is precise. The substance is Jesus.


The Resonance
Do you need a hero? Do you need a deliverer? Do you need a victor? Remember the seed of the woman. Remember Jesus. He is the hero. He is the deliverer. He is the victor.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for being the seed of the woman. Thank you for crushing the serpent's head. Thank you for defeating the enemy. Thank you for winning the victory. Help me to live in the victory you have won. Amen.

Jacob's ladder was a dream. It was a vision. It was a shadow of something greater.


The Ancient Text (OT)
"He had a dream in which he saw a stairway resting on the earth, with its top reaching to heaven, and the angels of God were ascending and descending on it." - Genesis 28:12 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


Jacob was running away. He was afraid. He was alone. He was in the wilderness. He used a stone for a pillow. He fell asleep. He dreamed. He saw a stairway. It was a stairway that connected heaven and earth. It was a stairway that connected God and man. It was a shadow. It pointed to a person. It pointed to a connection. It pointed to Jesus.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"He then added, 'Very truly I tell you, you will see "heaven open, and the angels of God ascending and descending on" the Son of Man.'" - John 1:51


Jesus is the stairway to heaven. He is the connection. He is the fulfillment of Jacob's ladder. He is the one who connects heaven and earth. He is the one who connects God and man. He is the way. He is the truth. He is the life.


The Verdict
Jacob's ladder was a shadow. It pointed to a person. It pointed to Jesus. The pattern is exact. The shadow is precise. The substance is Jesus.


The Resonance
Do you feel disconnected from God? Do you feel like there is a gap? Do you feel like there is a distance? Remember Jacob's ladder. Remember Jesus. He is the connection. He is the way. He is the bridge.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for being the stairway to heaven. Thank you for connecting me to God. Thank you for being the way. Thank you for being the bridge. Help me to walk in that connection. Amen.

"Then the LORD said to Moses, 'I will rain down bread from heaven for you. The people are to go out each day and gather enough for that day.'" - Exodus 16:4 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


The manna was a gift. It was a gift of provision. It was a gift of grace. The people were hungry. They were complaining. They were grumbling. God rained down bread from heaven. It appeared every morning. They gathered it. They ate it. They were satisfied. It was a shadow. It pointed to a person. It pointed to a bread. It pointed to Jesus.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"For the bread of God is the bread that comes down from heaven and gives life to the world." - John 6:33


Jesus is the manna from heaven. He is the bread of God. He is the bread that comes down from heaven. He is the bread that gives life to the world. He is the fulfillment of the manna. He is the true bread. He is the gift. He is the provision.


The Verdict
The manna was a shadow. It pointed to a person. It pointed to Jesus. The pattern is exact. The shadow is precise. The substance is Jesus.


The Resonance
Are you hungry? Are you hungry for the bread of God? Are you hungry for the bread that gives life? Remember the manna. Remember Jesus. He is the bread. He is the gift. He is the provision.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for being the manna from heaven. Thank you for being the bread of God. Thank you for being the bread that gives life. Feed me today. Satisfy my hunger. Amen.
pages.title: Day 29: The Manna from Heaven

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Hook
The law is a shadow. It is not the real thing. It is the shadow of something greater.


The Ancient Text (OT)
"The law is only a shadow of the good things that are coming—not the realities themselves. For this reason it can never, by the same sacrifices repeated endlessly year after year, make perfect those who draw near to worship." - Hebrews 10:1 (Written around 60 A.D.)


The law was a shadow. It was a shadow of the good things that are coming. It was a shadow of the realities themselves. It was a shadow of Jesus. The law could not make perfect. The sacrifices could not make perfect. The rituals could not make perfect. They were shadows. They were pointing to something greater. They were pointing to a person.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"These are a shadow of the things that were to come; the reality, however, is found in Christ." - Colossians 2:17


Jesus is the reality. He is the substance. He is the fulfillment of the shadow. He is the good thing that is coming. He is the perfect one. He is the one who makes perfect. He is the one who completes the shadow.


The Verdict
The law was a shadow. It pointed to a person. It pointed to Jesus. The pattern is exact. The shadow is precise. The substance is Jesus.


The Resonance
You have the real thing. You have Jesus. You do not need to keep looking at shadows. You do not need to keep living in the shadow. You can live in the reality. You can live in the substance. You can live in Christ.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for being the reality. Thank you for being the substance. Thank you for being the fulfillment of the shadow. Help me to stop living in the shadow. Help me to live in the reality. Help me to live in you. Amen.



END MATTER


The 30-Day Shadow Challenge
You have journeyed through 30 ancient shadows. Now what? I challenge you to read the book of Hebrews. It is 13 chapters. It is the perfect follow-up to this book. It will show you how Jesus is greater than the angels, greater than Moses, greater than the priests, and greater than the sacrifices. As you read, look for the shadows. Look for the substance. Look for Jesus.


A Note on Faith
The shadows are evidence. They are evidence of a divine plan. But evidence does not save you. The shadows point to a person. The shadows point to Jesus. You can understand the shadows and still miss the substance. The invitation is for your heart. Jesus said, "Here I am! I stand at the door and knock. If anyone hears my voice and opens the door, I will come in." The shadows are on the table. The door is open. It is your choice.


About the Author
Christine A. writes for the spiritually curious. He is passionate about showing people the hidden wisdom of the Bible. He lives with his family and enjoys good coffee and long conversations with skeptics. He believes that honest questions deserve honest answers.


Coming Next: The New Believer Edition
If you have made a decision to follow Jesus, the next step is to build a strong foundation. The New Believer Edition takes the same 30 shadows and shows you how to apply them to your new life. It is a 30 day guide to understanding what Jesus did for you. It will help you grow in your faith and trust in God.


Final Call to Action
Scan the QR code below to get the next book in the series. Visit our website to download a free reading plan. Join our community of seekers. The investigation is not over. The adventure is just beginning.
